note: Terms this project withdrew, with what to say instead, and a ceiling on how many times each may still appear. A withdrawal recorded only in the glossary withdraws nothing: carrier was withdrawn on 2026-10-12 and used 173 times afterwards, including in work done two days later. The ceiling may be lowered freely and never raised, so the uses already written into dated records can stand -- they are evidence of what was thought at the time -- while a new use fails the build.

terms.insteadSay: prov:Entity for the value, port type for what a connection is checked against, or the class the value already asserts
terms.why: Defined as a prov:Entity that travels between ports, then withdrawn when no standard could be shown that defines such a class. The definition was derivable rather than new, and nothing consumed it.

classified.why: The practitioner, 2026-10-15: "It's like 'carrier' which is still out there in several files" -- naming this debt as the same failure as a settled model that never reached the code. A ceiling that forbids a NEW use is not a plan to clear the old ones, so the count sat at 146 for three days and could have sat there indefinitely. Classifying it is what turns a cap into work.
classified.note: Dated records -- experiments, audits, research notes -- may never be reworded: a withdrawn term inside one is evidence of what was thought then, and 79 of the uses are those. Six more are necessary mentions: the ontology's own record that the term was withdrawn, and references to the fw:Carrier CLASS that D11 rejected, which is the name of a rejected artefact rather than a use of the vocabulary. The 4 live uses in ontology/fieldwork.ttl, validate-rulesets.mjs and validate-naming.mjs were reworded to 'port type' on 2026-10-15 and the ceiling fell 146 -> 142.
classified.whatRemains: The 57 in ledgers. widgets/blockers.json holds 21 and most are inside dated blocker entries, which are records; some are in live fields such as liftTest. Separating those is the next reduction and nobody has done it. The floor, once separated, is the dated-record count: below that the ceiling cannot fall without falsifying the record.
